key_idea: Expanding the square, the sum of i^2 over a permutation is constant, so only -2*sum(i_r*S_r) matters; by the rearrangement inequality sort results by their sum of positions.
sketch: Cost = sum_r (k*i_r^2 - 2*i_r*S_r + const) where S_r is the sum of r's positions over all engines. Since the i_r form a permutation of 1..n the quadratic term is fixed, so maximise sum i_r*S_r, i.e. give larger positions to larger S_r: sort ascending by S_r. Ties can be broken arbitrarily (any order is optimal); stable sort by id used. O(nk + n log n) with 5e5 input integers, so use fast input. Multiple answers are accepted; all three samples matched exactly and optimality follows from the rearrangement inequality.
